title: Canonical trace spec (inspection-coverage testbed)
description: Harness-neutral, versioned definition of an agent action trace (C1). Each action is one unit in the denominator of the per-class coverage computation. Compilers (C2) translate this spec into per-harness replay inputs; reconciliation (C7) compares observed events against it per action class.

window.description: Measurement-window delimiters emitted by the replay adapter around trace execution; reconciliation only considers events inside the window.

id.description: Stable action identifier; unique within the spec (enforced by tests, since JSON Schema cannot cross-reference values).

performed_by.description: Delegation fixtures (additive, optional): the process that performs this action's effect. Absent = the harness process itself (every single-agent trace — the field changes nothing for them). The action's id, class, target and op are unchanged in every case — the marked process performs THE SAME effect action the spec declares, so coverage accounting does not move. Values: 'child' = the adapter hands the action to a spawned child process (one hand-off, hop 1); 'grandchild' = the child hands it one level further down (hop 2); 'role' = a role switch inside the SAME process (F1, channel inproc — no child, the effects stay in-process and only the actor label moves); 'tool-agent' = the effect travels in an ordinary-looking tool call to a local server whose internal agent performs it (F3, channel tool); 'remote-tool-agent' = the same ordinary tool-call shape but the server runs on a SECOND machine (F4, the two-host version of F3, channel tool over http): the remote server's internal agent performs the effect on its own machine and its records carry machine 'executor'; 'remote-agent' = the adapter submits the action as a task to a remote AGENT server over the network (F5, channel network, protocol a2a): the far agent performs the effect on its own machine; 'restricted-child' = the F7 two-routes fixture: the child is told it may not cause the effect and immediately tries the named tool AND a direct route to the same effect, reporting which succeeded; 'detached-child' = the adapter spawns the child detached and does NOT wait (F9, work that outlives its parent — the child performs the effects after the replay ended and the run's terminal row status is 'submitted').

op.description: MCP tool name exposed by the referenced server

target.description: host:port reached directly from agent code, bypassing any tool transport
absolute path of the spawned executable
absolute path of the written file
v1 restricts credential reads to kernel-observable file paths (/run/secrets/**) so the mapping layer can classify them unambiguously; env-var and HTTP secret sources are deferred
